chunks: And among what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from Sayf ibn ʿAmīrah and Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
The iqamah is once, once, except for the phrase “Allah is the Greatest,” for it is twice.

So the explanation regarding these two reports is that they are a form of taqiyyah, because they agree with the doctrines of some of the general populace. And it is possible that the basis in them may be in a state of necessity and haste; and that which reveals what we have mentioned...

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity under sensitive circumstances
key_terms.اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ: the takbir phrase used in the iqamah
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةُ: the iqamah, the call immediately preceding salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: How is the iqamah counted in Shia hadith, and how are conflicting reports explained?
ai.summary: This report discusses the number of phrases in the iqamah, stating that its phrases are recited once each, except for “Allahu Akbar,” which is recited twice. The compiler then explains that the relevant reports may be understood as arising from taqiyyah or from circumstances of necessity and haste, indicating a juristic method for reconciling narrations.
